model.erp_analytics.int_ar_aging_buckets.name: int_ar_aging_buckets
model.erp_analytics.int_ar_aging_buckets.description: Intermediate accounts receivable outstanding balance aging buckets.
model.erp_analytics.int_ar_aging_buckets.raw_code:
WITH active_invoices AS (
    SELECT
        id AS invoice_id,
        invoice_no,
        customer_id,
        issue_date,
        due_date,
        grand_total,
        amount_paid,
        balance_due,
        status
    FROM {{ ref('stg_invoices') }}
    WHERE status IN ('issued', 'partially_paid')
      AND balance_due > 0
),
aging_calc AS (
    SELECT
        invoice_id,
        invoice_no,
        customer_id,
        issue_date,
        due_date,
        grand_total,
        amount_paid,
        balance_due,
        status,
        -- Days overdue calculation (relative to due date)
        CAST(CURRENT_DATE - due_date AS INTEGER) AS days_overdue
    FROM active_invoices
)
SELECT
    invoice_id,
    invoice_no,
    customer_id,
    issue_date,
    due_date,
    grand_total,
    amount_paid,
    balance_due,
    status,
    days_overdue,
    CASE
        WHEN days_overdue <= 0 THEN 'current'
        WHEN days_overdue BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30_days'
        WHEN days_overdue BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60_days'
        WHEN days_overdue BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90_days'
        ELSE 'over_90_days'
    END AS aging_bucket
FROM aging_calc

model.erp_analytics.int_customer_scd2.name: int_customer_scd2
model.erp_analytics.int_customer_scd2.description: Intermediate Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 representation of customers.
model.erp_analytics.int_customer_scd2.raw_code:
WITH raw_customers AS (
    SELECT
        id AS customer_id,
        customer_no,
        name,
        customer_type,
        status,
        industry,
        credit_limit,
        payment_terms_days,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        _extracted_at,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY id 
            ORDER BY updated_at ASC, _extracted_at ASC
        ) AS revision_no
    FROM {{ source('raw', 'customers') }}
),
with_validity AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        customer_no,
        name,
        customer_type,
        status,
        industry,
        credit_limit,
        payment_terms_days,
        updated_at AS valid_from,
        LEAD(updated_at) OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id 
            ORDER BY updated_at ASC, _extracted_at ASC
        ) AS valid_to,
        revision_no
    FROM raw_customers
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    customer_no,
    name,
    customer_type,
    status,
    industry,
    credit_limit,
    payment_terms_days,
    valid_from,
    valid_to,
    CASE WHEN valid_to IS NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_current
FROM with_validity

model.erp_analytics.dim_date.name: dim_date
model.erp_analytics.dim_date.description: Conformed calendar and fiscal date dimension.
model.erp_analytics.dim_date.raw_code:
WITH RECURSIVE dates AS (
    SELECT CAST('2023-01-01' AS DATE) AS full_date
    UNION ALL
    SELECT CAST(full_date + INTERVAL '1 day' AS DATE)
    FROM dates
    WHERE full_date < CAST('2026-12-31' AS DATE)
)
SELECT
    CAST(TO_CHAR(full_date, 'YYYYMMDD') AS INTEGER) AS date_key,
    full_date,
    CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(EXTRACT(MONTH FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    CAST(EXTRACT(DAY FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS day,
    CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_year,
    CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_quarter,
    CAST(EXTRACT(MONTH FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS fiscal_month,
    CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_quarter,
    CAST(EXTRACT(DOW FROM full_date) AS INTEGER) AS day_of_week,
    TRIM(TO_CHAR(full_date, 'Day')) AS day_name,
    TRIM(TO_CHAR(full_date, 'Month')) AS month_name,
    CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM full_date) IN (0, 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_weekend
FROM dates

model.erp_analytics.fact_sales_line.raw_code:
WITH erp_invoices AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(TO_CHAR(i.issue_date, 'YYYYMMDD') AS INTEGER) AS date_key,
        c.customer_key,
        p.product_key,
        1 AS source_system_key,
        i.invoice_no,
        'invoice' AS document_type,
        il.line_number,
        il.quantity,
        il.unit_price,
        il.subtotal AS gross,
        il.discount_amount AS discount,
        il.subtotal AS net_revenue,
        il.tax_amount AS tax
    FROM {{ ref('stg_invoices') }} i
    JOIN {{ ref('stg_invoice_lines') }} il ON i.id = il.invoice_id
    JOIN {{ ref('dim_customer') }} c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id AND c.is_current = TRUE
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('dim_product') }} p ON p.product_id = il.product_id
    WHERE i.status IN ('issued', 'partially_paid', 'paid')
)
SELECT 
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY invoice_no, line_number) AS sales_line_key,
    *
FROM erp_invoices

model.erp_analytics.stg_legacy_sales.name: stg_legacy_sales
model.erp_analytics.stg_legacy_sales.raw_code:
WITH date_extracted AS (
    SELECT 
        _raw_id,
        _file_name,
        _row_number,
        _extracted_at,
        _run_id,
        _source,
        invoice_no,
        order_date,
        legacy_customer_id,
        customer_name,
        sku,
        item_description,
        quantity,
        unit_price,
        total_amount,
        payment_status,
        -- Extract components based on format
        CASE 
            WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 7, 4) AS INT)
            ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 1, 4) AS INT)
        END AS _yr,
        CASE 
            WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 1, 2) AS INT)
            ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 6, 2) AS INT)
        END AS _mo,
        CASE 
            WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 4, 2) AS INT)
            ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(order_date, 9, 2) AS INT)
        END AS _dy,
        CASE 
            WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN SUBSTR(order_date, 7, 4) || '-' || SUBSTR(order_date, 1, 2) || '-' || SUBSTR(order_date, 4, 2)
            WHEN order_date LIKE '____.__.__' THEN REPLACE(order_date, '.', '-')
            ELSE order_date
        END AS _iso_date_str
    FROM {{ source('raw', 'legacy_sales') }}
),
validation AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        CASE 
            WHEN _mo BETWEEN 1 AND 12 AND _dy >= 1 AND _dy <= (
                CASE 
                    WHEN _mo IN (1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12) THEN 31
                    WHEN _mo IN (4, 6, 9, 11) THEN 30
                    WHEN _mo = 2 AND ((_yr % 4 = 0 AND _yr % 100 != 0) OR _yr % 400 = 0) THEN 29
                    ELSE 28
                END
            ) THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS _is_valid_date
    FROM date_extracted
)
SELECT 
    _raw_id,
    _file_name,
    _row_number,
    _extracted_at,
    _run_id,
    _source,
    invoice_no,
    order_date,
    legacy_customer_id,
    customer_name,
    sku,
    item_description,
    quantity,
    unit_price,
    total_amount,
    payment_status,
    -- Parsed attributes
    CASE WHEN _is_valid_date = 1 THEN _iso_date_str ELSE NULL END AS parsed_order_date,
    CAST(quantity AS NUMERIC) AS parsed_quantity,
    CAST(
        TRIM(
            REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(unit_price, '₱', ''), 'PHP', ''), ',', ''), ' ', '')
        ) AS NUMERIC
    ) AS parsed_unit_price,
    CAST(
        TRIM(
            REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(total_amount, '₱', ''), 'PHP', ''), ',', ''), ' ', '')
        ) AS NUMERIC
    ) AS parsed_total_amount,
    -- Parse error tracking
    CASE 
        WHEN _is_valid_date = 0 AND CAST(quantity AS NUMERIC) < 0 THEN 'invalid_order_date;negative_quantity'
        WHEN _is_valid_date = 0 THEN 'invalid_order_date'
        WHEN CAST(quantity AS NUMERIC) < 0 THEN 'negative_quantity'
        ELSE NULL
    END AS parse_error
FROM validation;

    select

      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      viewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,

    union all
    select distinct
     '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
     proname as name,
     ns.nspname as schema,
     'function' as type
    from pg_proc
     join pg_namespace as ns on pronamespace = ns.oid
    where ns.nspname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
  {% endcall %}
  {{ return(load_result('list_relations_without_caching').table) }}

{% macro postgres__get_show_indexes_sql(relation) %}
    select

        m.amname                                    as method,

    from pg_index ix
    join pg_class i

    join pg_am m

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_relations() -%}

  {#
      -- in pg_depend, objid is the dependent, refobjid is the referenced object
      --  > a pg_depend entry indicates that the referenced object cannot be
      --  > dropped without also dropping the dependent object.
  #}

  {%- call statement('relations', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select distinct
        dependent_namespace.nspname as dependent_schema,
        dependent_class.relname as dependent_name,
        referenced_namespace.nspname as referenced_schema,
        referenced_class.relname as referenced_name

    -- Query for views: views are entries in pg_class with an entry in pg_rewrite, but we avoid
    -- a seq scan on pg_rewrite by leveraging the fact there is an "internal" row in pg_depend for
    -- the view...
    from pg_class as dependent_class
    join pg_namespace as dependent_namespace on dependent_namespace.oid = dependent_class.relnamespace
    join pg_depend as dependent_depend on dependent_depend.refobjid = dependent_class.oid
        and dependent_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.deptype = 'i'

    -- ... and via pg_depend (that has a row per column, hence the need for "distinct" above, and
    -- making sure to exclude the internal row to avoid a view appearing to depend on itself)...
    join pg_depend as joining_depend on joining_depend.objid = dependent_depend.objid
        and joining_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refobjid != dependent_depend.refobjid

    -- ... we can find the tables they query from in pg_class, but excluding system tables. Note we
    -- don't need need to exclude _dependent_ system tables, because they only query from other
    -- system tables, and so are automatically excluded by excluding _referenced_ system tables
    join pg_class as referenced_class on referenced_class.oid = joining_depend.refobjid
    join pg_namespace as referenced_namespace on referenced_namespace.oid = referenced_class.relnamespace
        and referenced_namespace.nspname != 'information_schema'
        and referenced_namespace.nspname not like 'pg\_%'

    order by
        dependent_schema, dependent_name, referenced_schema, referenced_name;

  {%- endcall -%}

  {{ return(load_result('relations').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
